evidence.observation: The dependency path is checkout-web -> payment-api -> auth-gateway; the recent auth-gateway change AUTH-2026-0318 rotated the issuer and JWKS cache namespace for partner-token validation.

At 14:10Z, checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and 2400 ms p95 with notes that checkout submits were rejected after payment auth; payment-api had a 21.2% HTTP 401 rate and explicitly reported an invalid-issuer auth dependency; auth-gateway had a 28.4% HTTP 401 rate with issuer mismatch.
After AUTH-2026-0318 deployed at 14:05:12Z, auth-gateway logged a JWKS cache miss and then rejected token issuer partner-v2 because only partner-v1 was allowed.
Payment API token validation failed with issuer_not_allowed and create_payment was rejected as invalid_issuer, matching the checkout failure path.
Checkout submit_order failed with HTTP 401 from payment-api, and the flow remained blocked even though static assets recovered.
Orders DB reported normal 35 ms query p95, zero errors, and no failed checkout transaction reached the database for the failing request.

excluded_red_herrings.signal: orders-db CPU at 86% during vacuum maintenance
excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: Query p95 was normal at 35 ms with zero errors, and the failing checkout request was rejected before reaching orders-db.
The metric notes isolate those errors to images; checkout logs say static assets served normally after retry while the checkout flow remained blocked on payment authorization.
These are downstream effects of repeated authentication failures, not evidence of a database or frontend-originated cause; both services identify invalid issuer/auth dependency failures.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately roll back AUTH-2026-0318 or restore partner-v2 in auth-gateway allowed_issuers, then invalidate or refresh the affected JWKS cache namespace as appropriate.
Verify auth-gateway accepts a known-good partner-v2 token and that payment-api create_payment succeeds for a controlled checkout request.
Verify checkout-web HTTP 401 rate and p95 return toward baseline, confirm new checkout submits succeed, and monitor auth-gateway issuer-mismatch and JWKS-cache-miss errors.
After stabilization, review the issuer allowlist and JWKS namespace migration for an atomic configuration/deployment process and add a compatibility test for partner-v2 tokens.
